observations.text: SP executed the breakout at the code desired for the Training Section, initiating the turn away from the formation only after the IP directed it and with the IP applying part of the bank input to ensure separation of the A/C flight path. The call to the formation leader was made by the IP on both occasions the maneuver was imposed, and altitude deviation during the turn away reached 340 feet. Performance is marginal for the block; an unprompted turn away from the formation flight path and a timely call to the leader are expected to develop in the following sorties.

SP initiated the breakout turn away from the formation after the IP's verbal prompt and flew the maneuver with no control input from the IP. Separation of the A/C flight path was established, with altitude deviation held at 300 feet and exit heading 10 degrees from the briefed value, at the code 1 limits. Recognition of the condition imposing the breakout was delayed, but the control inputs and the call to the formation leader were made by SP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP recognized the loss of visual contact with the formation leader and executed the breakout without IP's intervention, turning away from the formation flight path and informing the leader on the briefed frequency. A late power reduction in the turn away was identified and corrected by SP in a timely manner, with the result of an airspeed deviation of 15 knots and an altitude deviation of 210 feet, between the code 3 and code 1 limits. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP applied timely and proper control inputs when the breakout was ordered by the formation leader, ensuring separation of the A/C flight path and informing the leader within the same turn. Altitude was held within 100 feet, airspeed within 8 knots and exit heading within 4 degrees of the briefed values, inside the code 3 limits, and no IP intervention was necessary. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the breakout exactly as prescribed by the Techniques and Procedures Manual on every occasion it was imposed, starting the turn away from the formation flight path at the first indication of the developing condition. Altitude deviation did not exceed 40 feet, airspeed 3 knots and exit heading 2 degrees, and the call to the formation leader was passed within the first seconds of the maneuver. Separation of the flight paths was established well clear of the leader's 3/9 line and no prompting was required at any point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an initial roll input made toward the formation leader instead of away from him, did not apply the control inputs required to ensure separation of the A/C flight path. The IP took the controls and flew part of the turn away, with the result that lateral separation was regained only after the aircraft had crossed the leader's 3/9 line and altitude deviation exceeded 400 feet.

SP, due to a startle response that displaced the memorised sequence, did not initiate the breakout when the formation leader ordered it and remained in position while closure continued. The IP directed the maneuver and applied part of the control inputs to establish separation of the flight paths, with the result of an altitude deviation beyond 300 feet and no call passed to the formation leader by SP.

SP executed the breakout at the code desired for the Training Section, initiating the turn away from the formation only after the IP's verbal prompt on both occasions it was imposed. The maneuver itself was flown without IP's intervention, with an altitude deviation of 290 feet and an exit heading 9 degrees from the briefed value, and the call to the leader followed the control inputs by about five seconds. Performance is marginal for the block; unprompted recognition of the conditions that impose a breakout is expected to improve.

SP recognized the developing closure on the formation leader and executed the breakout without IP's intervention, turning away from the formation flight path and informing the leader. A momentarily excessive bank input was identified and corrected by SP in a timely manner, with the result of an altitude deviation of 230 feet and an airspeed deviation of 14 knots, between the code 3 and code 1 limits. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP applied timely and proper control inputs on every occasion the breakout was imposed, ensuring separation of the A/C flight path and informing the formation leader in time. Deviations were held within 130 feet of altitude, 9 knots of airspeed and 4 degrees of exit heading, inside the code 3 limits, and the IP's intervention was not necessary. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the breakout flawlessly whenever it was imposed, with the turn away from the formation started at the first indication of the condition and the call to the formation leader passed together with the control inputs. Altitude deviation remained within 50 feet, airspeed within 4 knots and exit heading within 2 degrees. Separation of the A/C flight path was established immediately and no IP prompting was needed at any point in the sortie. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a breakout turn flown with insufficient bank and without the accompanying power reduction, did not ensure separation of the A/C flight path from that of the formation leader. The IP intervened on the controls to increase the rate of turn away, with the result that the aircraft passed in front of the leader's 3/9 line and altitude deviation exceeded 350 feet.

SP, due to lack of assertiveness in voicing a recognised unsafe condition, did not execute the breakout when visual contact with the formation leader was lost, continuing to fly the last known relative position. The IP directed the maneuver and flew part of the turn away to establish separation of the flight paths, with the result that no call was passed to the formation leader and the exit heading finished 25 degrees from the briefed value.

SP, due to a delayed reading of the closure developing in the turn, did not initiate the breakout until the IP called for it verbally. The maneuver was then flown without IP's intervention, with the result of an altitude deviation of 300 feet and an exit heading 10 degrees from the briefed value, at the code 1 limits, and the call to the formation leader was passed only after the aircraft was already clear.

SP, due to an indirect hint instead of a direct statement of the aircraft state, did not inform the formation leader in time that a breakout was being flown, and started the turn away only after the IP's verbal prompt. Separation of the A/C flight path was then achieved by SP alone, with the result of an airspeed deviation of 20 knots at the code 1 limit and a call to the leader delayed by about eight seconds.

SP executed the breakout within the desired standards for the Training Section, turning away from the formation flight path without IP's intervention on both occasions it was imposed. Minor errors in power management were self-corrected in a timely manner, with airspeed deviations of 18 knots on the first breakout and 15 knots on the second, close to the code 1 limit, and an altitude deviation of 240 feet. Performance is marginal for the block; tighter airspeed and altitude control during the turn away is expected to improve.

SP applied timely and proper control inputs when the breakout was ordered by the formation leader, ensuring separation of the A/C flight path and passing the required call in time. Altitude was held within 140 feet, airspeed within 10 knots and exit heading within 5 degrees, inside the code 3 limits, without any IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the breakout exactly as prescribed by the Techniques and Procedures Manual, initiating the turn away at the first indication of the developing situation and informing the formation leader in the same instant. Altitude deviation did not exceed 45 feet, airspeed 4 knots and exit heading 2 degrees, and separation of the A/C flight path was established well before the leader's 3/9 line. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a nose-high turn away that allowed the airspeed to decay while bank was being increased, did not execute the breakout in a manner that ensured separation of the A/C flight path. The IP took the controls and completed the maneuver, with the result of an airspeed deviation beyond 20 knots and an altitude deviation of 380 feet.

SP, due to degraded situational awareness after the unplanned change of sequence, did not identify that a breakout was imposed when visual contact with the formation leader was lost, and held the previous relative position. The IP directed the turn away and applied part of the control inputs, with the result that separation of the flight paths was established late and the exit heading finished 30 degrees from the briefed value. No call was passed to the formation leader by SP.

SP, due to an imprecise application of bank and power in the turn away, did not fly the breakout to completion without prompting, requiring the IP's verbal directions on bank angle and power setting. The deviations were recognized and corrected with delay, with the result of an altitude deviation of 300 feet and an exit heading 10 degrees from the briefed value, at the code 1 limits.

SP, due to absent inquiry when the observed aircraft performance did not match the expected, did not question the increasing closure on the formation leader and delayed the breakout until the IP called for it. The maneuver was then flown by SP without IP's intervention, with the result of an airspeed deviation of 20 knots at the code 1 limit and a call to the leader passed only after separation of the flight path had been achieved.

SP, due to a late power reduction during the turn away, did not hold the briefed airspeed while establishing separation of the A/C flight path. The error was recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP's intervention, with the result of an airspeed deviation of 16 knots and an altitude deviation of 220 feet, between the code 3 and code 1 limits.

SP, due to distraction from the primary scan by an unrelated switch action, did not inform the formation leader immediately after initiating the breakout. The omission was recognized by SP and the call was passed a few seconds later without IP prompting, with the result of an exit heading 8 degrees from the briefed value and an altitude deviation of 200 feet, between the code 3 and code 1 limits.

SP executed the breakout timely and without IP's intervention on each occasion it was imposed, applying proper control inputs to ensure separation of the A/C flight path and informing the formation leader. Deviations remained inside the code 3 limits but at their upper edge, with altitude 145 feet, airspeed 10 knots and exit heading 5 degrees on the second breakout. Performance is marginal for the Training Section; a wider margin within the desired standards is expected in the following sorties.

SP executed the breakout flawlessly whenever it was imposed, applying proper control inputs at the first indication and informing the formation leader in the same transmission. Altitude deviation did not exceed 40 feet, airspeed 3 knots and exit heading 2 degrees, and separation of the A/C flight path was established with no closure on the leader at any moment. Lookout and control discipline throughout the maneuver were above the level expected at this stage of training. Above end of block MIF achieved.
